digest.lead: Claude Code v2.1.90 ships with interactive learning features and stability fixes, while the developer community experiments with JAX-based alternatives.
digest.summary: Meanwhile, discussions continue around content filtering policies and broader competitive dynamics in the AI landscape.

stories.headline: Anthropic Content Filter Blocks 'OpenClaw' References
stories.summary: Users discovered that Anthropic has implemented content filtering that blocks references to 'OpenClaw' [1]. The finding sparked discussion about content moderation policies and potential competitive sensitivities.
stories.impact: This affects users who may encounter unexpected content blocks when discussing or referencing certain terms, highlighting the boundaries of Anthropic's content policies.

sources.title: Anthropic has a blacklist on the word "OpenClaw"

stories.headline: Claude Code v2.1.90 Introduces Interactive Learning and Stability Improvements
stories.summary: The latest Claude Code release adds `/powerup` interactive lessons with animated demos to help users learn features more effectively [1]. The update also includes offline environment improvements and fixes for critical issues like infinite rate-limit dialogs that could crash sessions [1].
key_points: New `/powerup` command provides interactive tutorials with animated demonstrations
Enhanced offline support with `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_KEEP_MARKETPLACE_ON_FAILURE` environment variable
Fixed session-crashing infinite loop in rate-limit dialogs
stories.impact: This update significantly improves the onboarding experience for new Claude Code users while addressing stability issues that affected daily workflows for existing developers.

stories.headline: Nanocode Project Offers JAX-Based Alternative to Claude Code on TPUs
stories.summary: A community developer has created Nanocode, positioning it as 'the best Claude Code that $200 can buy' using pure JAX implementation on TPUs [1]. The project has gained significant attention in the developer community, suggesting interest in cost-effective alternatives to official tooling.
key_points: Implements Claude Code functionality using JAX on TPU infrastructure
Claims significant cost advantages at around $200
Pure JAX implementation may offer performance benefits for specific use cases
stories.impact: This demonstrates the community's drive to create cost-effective alternatives to official Claude tooling, particularly relevant for developers and teams with budget constraints or specific performance requirements.

sources.title: Nanocode: The best Claude Code that $200 can buy in pure JAX on TPUs

stories.headline: Enable PowerShell tool for Windows development workflows
stories.summary: Claude Code now includes an opt-in PowerShell tool that allows Windows users to execute PowerShell commands directly through Claude. This provides native Windows command-line access for system administration and development tasks.
actionable_steps: Update Claude Code to version 2.1.84 or later
Enable the PowerShell tool in your settings as a preview feature

stories.headline: Use forceRemoteSettingsRefresh policy to ensure fresh configuration on startup
stories.summary: This setting forces Claude Code CLI to fetch the latest remote managed settings before starting and exits if the fetch fails. This ensures your CLI always runs with the most current configuration and prevents running with stale settings that might cause issues.
actionable_steps: Open your Claude Code CLI configuration
Restart the CLI to verify it blocks startup until fresh settings are fetched

stories.headline: Use managed settings drop-in directory for team policy deployment
stories.summary: The new managed-settings.d/ directory allows multiple teams to deploy independent configuration fragments that automatically merge. This enables better organization of team-specific policies without conflicts.
actionable_steps: Create a managed-settings.d/ directory alongside your managed-settings.json
Place individual team policy files in the directory (they merge alphabetically)
Name files with prefixes to control merge order (e.g., 01-team-a.json, 02-team-b.json)

stories.headline: Use @-mentions to give Claude Code precise file context
stories.summary: Boris Cherny, creator of Claude Code, recommends using @-mentions to point Claude at specific files instead of letting it search. This dramatically reduces token usage and improves accuracy since Claude works with the exact files you intend rather than guessing from project structure.
actionable_steps: Type @ in Claude Code to see a file picker with fuzzy search
Select the specific files relevant to your task before writing your prompt
Combine multiple @-mentions for cross-file tasks like refactoring

stories.headline: Add session tracking header for proxy aggregation
stories.summary: Use the `X-Claude-Code-Session-Id` header in your API requests to help proxies group requests by session without needing to parse request bodies. This improves routing and monitoring capabilities when using Claude Code through proxy servers.
actionable_steps: Add the `X-Claude-Code-Session-Id` header to your Claude Code API requests
Set the header value to your session identifier
Configure your proxy to use this header for request aggregation instead of body parsing
